name: Dify
description: Platform for building AI agents, workflows, RAG applications and internal AI applications — being evaluated as a possible foundation for internal WASL AI agents.
tagline: Build and manage internal AI agents, workflows, and RAG apps.
useCases: Business Analyst Agent
Product Manager Agent
User Story Generator
User Story Review
Business Gap Analysis
Compliance Agent
Banking Knowledge Agent
Marketing Agent
Workflow Agent
deploymentNotes: Designed for self-hosting via Docker/Docker Compose (or Kubernetes with community Helm charts). Cloud requirement: compute for hosting plus API access to a configured LLM provider (proposed: Azure OpenAI).
license: Apache-2.0 (verify current terms on the upstream repository before any deployment decision)
problem: Teams across WASL repeatedly want to build AI-assisted workflows and agents but have no shared, supported platform to do this safely and consistently. Each team either builds one-off scripts or does nothing.
whatItDoes: Dify is an open-source LLM application development platform. It provides a visual workflow builder for orchestrating AI agents and pipelines, a way to build Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) applications over custom document sets, a plugin/tool-calling framework for connecting agents to external systems, and a hosted UI for prompt/workflow management and observability. It supports multiple LLM providers rather than locking WASL into one vendor.
whyEvaluating: If evaluation succeeds, Dify could become a shared, centrally supported platform for building internal AI agents and RAG applications, rather than every department building bespoke, unreviewed tooling. Centralizing on one reviewed platform makes it far easier to apply consistent security and compliance controls across every AI agent use case at once.
architecture: Self-hostable web application (Docker/Docker Compose is the common path) with a backend API, a workflow/orchestration engine, a vector database integration layer for RAG, and a web front end. It can call out to various LLM providers via configured API keys/endpoints, including Azure OpenAI.
dataConsiderations: Data requirements depend entirely on which use case is pursued. A RAG-style knowledge agent would need access to whatever document set it is meant to answer questions over — which must be limited to non-sensitive or explicitly approved data until a Security and Compliance review is complete.
securityNotes: Dify has not yet undergone a formal WASL Security Review. Open questions include: how the self-hosted deployment handles authentication/authorization for internal users, how uploaded RAG documents are stored and whether they're encrypted at rest, what data (if any) is sent to third-party model providers versus staying within a self-hosted/Azure boundary, and the project's history of security advisories. Provisional classification: Medium Risk, pending review.
complianceNotes: Not yet reviewed by Compliance/Legal. This project has not been assessed for SAMA relevance and must not be described as compliant with any regulatory framework until that review happens. License terms (Apache-2.0, to be reverified) should also be checked against WASL's open-source usage policy.
dataResidencyNotes: Not yet verified. If self-hosted on Azure infrastructure within a Saudi Arabia region, data residency could plausibly be maintained — but this requires explicit technical verification during Security Review, not assumption.
howToUse: This project is not yet approved for employee use. It is being evaluated. Interested employees should use Request Access below to register interest and help prioritize the evaluation.
pocStatus: No POC has been conducted yet. This entry reflects Initial AI Review only.

name: AnythingLLM
description: Potential internal ChatGPT-style knowledge assistant for WASL employees, with workspaces, RAG and access controls — being evaluated as a possible internal WASL GPT.
tagline: A self-hosted, ChatGPT-style assistant over approved internal knowledge.
useCases: WASL Knowledge workspace
Banking workspace
Product workspace
Business Analysis workspace
Compliance workspace
Finance workspace
HR workspace
Marketing workspace
Technology workspace
deploymentNotes: Designed for self-hosting via Docker, with a desktop app also available for local single-user use. Cloud requirement: compute, an LLM provider (proposed: Azure OpenAI), and a vector database.
license: MIT (verify current terms on the upstream repository before any deployment decision)
problem: Employees frequently need to find answers buried in internal documentation, policies, product specs, and departmental knowledge — but that knowledge is scattered across systems and hard to search.
whatItDoes: AnythingLLM is an open-source, self-hostable application that provides a ChatGPT-like chat interface backed by custom knowledge bases. It supports isolated 'workspaces' that keep different document sets and conversations separate, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over uploaded documents, multi-user accounts with role-based access control, and support for multiple LLM providers (including Azure OpenAI) and vector database backends.
whyEvaluating: If evaluation succeeds, AnythingLLM could become an internal, WASL-controlled alternative to public consumer AI chat tools for answering questions against approved internal documentation, with workspace isolation scoping different knowledge sets to different departments or sensitivity levels.
architecture: Self-hostable application (Docker) with a chat front end, a document ingestion/embedding pipeline, a pluggable vector database layer, and connectors to LLM providers.
dataConsiderations: Whatever documents are uploaded to a given workspace become searchable within that workspace. Document sets must be limited to non-sensitive or explicitly approved data until a Security and Compliance review is complete — especially important for the proposed Banking, Finance, and Compliance workspaces.
securityNotes: AnythingLLM has not yet undergone a formal WASL Security Review. Open questions include workspace-level access control granularity, how uploaded documents are stored and whether they're encrypted at rest, and what data (if any) leaves the self-hosted boundary when calling an LLM provider. Provisional classification: Medium Risk — likely to be reassessed per workspace, since a Banking or Compliance workspace would carry materially higher risk than a general FAQ workspace.
complianceNotes: Not yet reviewed by Compliance/Legal. This project has not been assessed for SAMA relevance and must not be described as compliant with any regulatory framework until that review happens, particularly for any workspace touching banking or financial documentation.
dataResidencyNotes: Not yet verified. If self-hosted on Azure infrastructure within a Saudi Arabia region with an in-region vector database and Azure OpenAI deployment, data residency could plausibly be maintained — but this requires explicit technical verification during Security Review.
howToUse: This project is not yet approved for employee use. It is being evaluated. Interested employees should use Request Access below to register interest and help prioritize the evaluation.
pocStatus: No POC has been conducted yet. This entry reflects Initial AI Review only.

Generate test cases from a user story before development starts
Generate a release checklist for an upcoming deployment
exampleWorkflow: GitHub PR -> n8n Trigger -> Dev Review Agent -> Code Review -> Test Suggestions -> Risk / Security Suggestions -> Comment on PR for a human reviewer to confirm or dismiss.

suggestedArchitecture.replit: Optional dashboard for reviewing agent-flagged PRs and test suggestions outside of GitHub itself.
suggestedArchitecture.n8n: Triggered by GitHub/Azure DevOps PR webhooks, orchestrates the review pipeline, and posts comments back to the PR.
suggestedArchitecture.azureOpenAI: Performs the code review analysis, generates test cases, and drafts release checklists.
suggestedArchitecture.azureAISearch: Optional: retrieval over WASL coding standards/security guidelines to ground review comments.

deploymentNotes: Proposed as an n8n workflow triggered by GitHub/Azure DevOps webhooks, with Azure OpenAI performing the analysis and posting suggestions as PR comments for human review. No repository integration has been set up — concept only.
problem: Engineering teams spend significant reviewer time on routine first-pass code review and manually writing test cases from user stories, slowing down delivery.
whatItDoes: A proposed AI agent that reviews pull requests for code quality, potential bugs, and API design issues, generates test cases from user stories, suggests release checklists, and posts its findings as PR comments — always as suggestions for a human reviewer, never as an automatic merge/approval.
whyEvaluating: If evaluation succeeds, this could speed up the review cycle by giving human reviewers an AI first pass to work from, while final approval and merge decisions remain entirely human.
architecture: Proposed shared-platform architecture: Employee -> WASL Marketplace / Replit App -> n8n -> Agent Logic -> Azure OpenAI + Azure AI Search + approved internal systems -> Output / Action / Human Approval. See /web/docs/architecture.md for the full shared-platform design.
dataConsiderations: This agent would read source code and PR metadata. Only WASL-owned repositories with appropriate access controls should be connected; no external/public exposure of proprietary code.
securityNotes: This agent has not yet undergone a formal WASL Security Review. Provisional classification only, pending review.
complianceNotes: Not yet reviewed by Compliance/Legal. This concept has not been assessed for SAMA relevance and must not be described as compliant with any regulatory framework, approved, or production-ready until that review happens.
dataResidencyNotes: Not yet verified. If built on Azure infrastructure within a Saudi Arabia region with in-region Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search deployments, data residency could plausibly be maintained — but this requires explicit technical verification during Security Review.
howToUse: This agent is a Research-stage concept only. It is not built and not available for employee use. Interested employees should use Request Access below to register interest and help prioritize which agent gets built first.
pocStatus: No POC has been conducted yet. This entry reflects an initial concept write-up only.

name: WASL BD Intelligence Agent
description: Helps research companies, identify opportunities, and prepare partnership actions — company research, opportunity scoring, and meeting briefings.
tagline: Type a company name, get a partnership-ready briefing.
useCases: Employee enters a company name and receives a company overview, market position, and partnership fit analysis
Generate meeting-prep questions ahead of a partner meeting
Draft a follow-up message after a BD meeting for human review before sending
exampleWorkflow: Employee enters company: "Tabby" -> Agent returns: Company overview, Products, Market position, Potential WASL opportunity, Partnership fit, Meeting questions, Suggested next actions — for a human BD team member to act on.

suggestedArchitecture.replit: UI for entering a company name and viewing the generated research briefing and suggested actions.
suggestedArchitecture.n8n: Orchestrates research retrieval, creates CRM tasks, and routes drafted follow-ups for human approval before sending.
suggestedArchitecture.azureOpenAI: Synthesizes company research into an overview, opportunity score, and partnership fit analysis.
suggestedArchitecture.azureAISearch: Optional: retrieval over WASL's own past partnership notes/CRM history for continuity across meetings.

deploymentNotes: Proposed as a Replit UI with n8n handling research retrieval and CRM task creation, and Azure OpenAI synthesizing the briefing. No CRM or external data source has been connected — concept only.
problem: Business Development and Partnerships teams spend significant manual time researching companies and preparing for partnership meetings, with no shared AI-assisted research tooling.
whatItDoes: A proposed AI agent that, given a company name, researches its products and market position from approved public/business sources, scores potential partnership fit with WASL, drafts meeting-prep questions, and suggests next actions — with any outbound communication or CRM action requiring human review before it is sent or committed.
whyEvaluating: If evaluation succeeds, this could speed up BD research and meeting prep significantly, while keeping outreach, follow-ups, and partnership decisions under human control.
architecture: Proposed shared-platform architecture: Employee -> WASL Marketplace / Replit App -> n8n -> Agent Logic -> Azure OpenAI + Azure AI Search + approved internal systems -> Output / Action / Human Approval. See /web/docs/architecture.md for the full shared-platform design.
dataConsiderations: This agent should only use approved public/business information sources. No confidential partner data or internal deal terms should be processed until Security and Compliance review is complete.
